legend: A mathematician from ancient times left behind a riddle for future generations. Carved into stone lies a challenge about numbers and operations : Any number can be represented using a sequence of +%%ZSMJ0%% and −%%ZSMJ1%% signs applied to the numbers 1, 2, 3, ...
You, a bright and curious mind from the future, decide to take up this challenge and makes it even more challenging.
Given an integer X%%ZSMJ2%%, your task is to express it in the form 1±2±3±4±…±N%%ZSMJ3%% so that the result equals X%%ZSMJ4%% and N%%ZSMJ5%% is the smallest number.
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ6%% (1≤t≤1000%%ZSMJ7%%) — the number of test cases.
Each testcase contains a single line of one integer X%%ZSMJ8%% ( |X|≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ9%% )
It is guaranteed that the sum |X|%%ZSMJ10%% over all test cases does not exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ11%%.
output: First, print a line with an integer N%%ZSMJ12%%.
Then print one valid expression in the format 1+2−3+4−5…N%%ZSMJ13%%. No spaces are allowed, and the sequence must include all numbers from 1%%ZSMJ14%% to N%%ZSMJ15%%.
If there are many expressions, output any of them.
